newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-HENMAN, IVANISEVIC IN FINE FORM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN, IVANISEVIC IN FINE FORM.

text.p: Defending champion Goran Ivanisevic and British number one Tim Henman served up a flurry of aces on Wednesday to overcome their respective opponents in straight sets at the Milan indoor tennis tournament.
Ivanisevic, the top seed, fired 22 aces past Cedric Pioline but needed tie-breaks to dismiss the Frenchman 7-6 7-6 in their second round encounter.
"I feel well and I am starting to serve to my full potential," the Croat said. "I think I can make it to the finals."
Ivanisevic has a 19-3 record in 1997 but was forced to withdraw from the European Community championship in Antwerp last week due to tendinitis in his left shoulder.
Henman, runner-up to Switzerland's Marc Rosset in Antwerp, his third ATP Tour final of the year, was almost as devastating in his first round match.
He delivered 13 aces as he brushed aside Adrian Voinea of Romania in just 44 minutes to win 6-1 6-2, although Voinea contributed to his own downfall with a string of unforced errors.
"Against Voinea I played better than in all the matches in Antwerp last week," Henman said.
Henman, ranked 14th in the world, now faces Petr Korda of the Czech Republic on Thursday. Korda defeated Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev 6-3 6-3.
Sergi Bruguera followed up his first round dismissal of Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek by beating fellow Spaniard Javier Sanchez 6-4 6-0.
Daniel Vacek of the Czech Republic defeated his countryman Bohdan Ulihrach 7-6 6-3 and will face Ivanisevic on Friday.
